name: MK-677 for appetite/sleep

card.summary: Use of the investigational oral growth hormone secretagogue MK-677 (ibutamoren), which mimics ghrelin, with the aim of more appetite and deeper sleep to support eating, recovery and muscle gain.
card.note: Investigational and not approved for human use in the US; case reports describe liver injury and hormonal side effects.

quick.overview:
MK-677 (ibutamoren) is an experimental oral drug that acts on the ghrelin receptor and raises growth hormone and IGF-1. Because ghrelin is the hunger hormone, and the drug increased REM and slow-wave sleep in a small human study, some users take it for stronger appetite and better sleep to support eating enough and recovering from training.

The chain to appearance is: more appetite and more sleep, then more eating and recovery, then more lean mass. Randomised trials in older adults found increased fat-free mass; users report hunger and sleep effects.
quick.how: People who use it describe it as an oral compound taken by mouth, often in the evening, and discuss appetite and sleep changes as the main early effects. This article does not give dosing or sourcing; the compound is an investigational drug, not an approved medicine.
quick.risks: Because the drug raises GH and IGF-1 and stimulates ghrelin signalling, researchers have measured effects on appetite, body composition and glucose handling. Case reports describe hepatotoxicity (2025) and reversible gynecomastia and hypogonadism with a performance supplement. It is an Investigational New Drug in the US and banned in most sports.

lead: MK-677, also called ibutamoren, is an orally active, non-peptide agonist of the ghrelin receptor that stimulates growth hormone release and raises IGF-1 [1][2]. It is an investigational drug and has not been approved for marketing for human use in the US [6].

Appetite and sleep are the two effects most associated with this use. Ghrelin signalling stimulates hunger, and an early controlled study reported improved sleep quality with prolonged MK-677 treatment [4]. In a randomised trial of healthy older adults, an oral ghrelin mimetic increased fat-free mass [3].
People who use MK-677 within bodybuilding and looksmaxxing circles discuss it as a way to eat more and sleep better while training. Case reports describe adverse effects in such users [7][8].

chain: Ghrelin-receptor agonism raises appetite and GH
More recovery and lean mass over time
angle.text: Users take MK-677 for the appetite and sleep effects as inputs to training, with gains in lean mass reported in older-adult trials.

infobox: Investigational; not approved for human use in the US

paras: MK-677 acts at the ghrelin receptor, the same target as the hunger hormone [5]. A two-month trial in obese subjects reported increased GH secretion, fat-free mass and energy expenditure [9]. A trial in dieters found MK-677 reversed diet-induced protein catabolism in eight volunteers on a calorie-restricted regimen [10].
In a 1997 controlled study, prolonged oral MK-677 improved sleep quality in men [4]. Summary reports of this work describe increased REM sleep and, in young subjects, slow-wave sleep [6].

A 2025 BMJ Case Reports article describes hepatotoxicity induced by MK-677 [7]. A 2024 case report describes reversible gynecomastia and hypogonadism after a commercial performance-enhancing supplement [8].

Randomised and controlled studies have examined MK-677 for GH/IGF-1 stimulation in healthy elderly subjects [11], body composition in older adults [3], diet-induced catabolism [10], sleep [4], bone turnover [12] and Alzheimer disease progression, where no clinical effect was found [13]. The Alzheimer trial registered 512 participants [14]. A Phase 3 trial of LUM-201 in children with GH deficiency began in 2026 [15].

timeline.event: Study reports GH/IGF-1 stimulation by daily oral MK-677 in healthy elderly subjects [11].
Controlled study reports improved sleep quality [4].
Trial in healthy older adults reports increased fat-free mass [3].
